bluf: OuterBox is an independent US growth and performance agency headquartered in Copley, OH, founded 2004, leading with SEO and web build for mid market ecommerce and calling itself the #1 ranked SEO company with 1,000+ clients over 20+ years. The record shows it buying paid media and analytics depth (TopSpot, Accelerated Digital Media, GRO Marketing) while publishing at pace: 178 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days, plus an llms.txt. A rival should know it sells paid social and CRO with no social pixel and no testing tool on its own site, lists SEO Packages but no prices, and reads Neutral on Horus at 6.2.
doing:
The positioning line reads full service performance marketing agency, strongest in ecommerce, delivering SEO and GEO, paid media, CRO, email and web design end to end: in plain words, a search and web build shop for mid market retailers that bought media and analytics. The headline claim, #1 ranked SEO company with 1,000+ clients over 20+ years, is quoted as a claim.

The sold mix leads with SEO (score 3: title and meta lead with it; JEGS and Soccer Innovations cases) and Web & Product (score 3: ecommerce, custom and B2B design pages; FANUC, Wine Enthusiast). Scoring 2: AI Search / GEO (a 2026-09-16 study on SEO foundations growing AI driven revenue for three brands), CRO (AICPA personalization), Data & Measurement (proprietary Loop Analytics, call tracking, the Kapp Alloy case), Email & CRM (Salesforce, Klaviyo, HubSpot, Mailchimp; Lang Antiques), Paid Search (a Caraway Performance Max case) and Paid Social (Save the Children Meta ROAS up 54%; Cue Health Advantage+ cut CPA 30%). Creator & Influencer scores 0; no partners are listed.

Its AI posture: GEO as an extension of SEO, plus AI chatbot and agent development, and LinkedIn ads offering AI visibility checks; 2026-09-24 articles cover prompt tracking and why we built obxfrontier, but no audited AI visibility product is on record. Moves by release date (the move list carries a second date per deal): TopSpot, a Houston SEO and paid media agency for industrial manufacturing (2025-07-21; move list 2024-06); Accelerated Digital Media for paid media, analytics and CRO (2025-10-21; move list 2026-09); GRO Marketing for senior, student and multi family housing (2026-01-22; move list 2026-05); Matt Prater appointed EVP of Innovation (2026-01-27); Jeff Hirz promoted to Chief Revenue Officer (2026-03-10); Vice President promotions for Blankenship and Commisso (2026-03-12). Pricing: the nav lists SEO Packages, no prices. Conspicuously absent: partners, a retail media line and an ATS; 8 open roles are listed, all search, paid media and email strategists.
clients:

As a judgment tied to the edition, this base of retailers, manufacturers and healthcare and housing lead buyers is likely to ask next for AI visibility proof and cheaper paid social (KJ1, the citation replacing the click; KJ6, the hollowed middle), moderate confidence.

openings: The contradiction to lead with: it sells paid social and CRO while its site runs no social ad pixel and no testing tool. A CRO or paid social pitch built on that say and do gap is likely to win the comparison for mid market ecommerce accounts, moderate confidence; the falsifier is a testing tool or Meta pixel on outerboxdesign.com at the next compile. Second, it sells GEO, publishes llms.txt and advertises AI visibility checks on LinkedIn, yet no audited product (citation share, scorecard, tracking) is on record, so a rival leading with an audited number is likely to beat a free check, moderate confidence. Third, no feed, schema or entity work sits on its core search and web lines, an unclaimed offer for its ecommerce book. Fourth, no public pricing beyond a nav item reading SEO Packages, so transparent outcome pricing is a conversation it cannot hold. The contestable accounts are the 5 names only slugs and Save the Children, which sdim also lists; the vertical to press is the acquired housing and senior living book. Most exposed to KJ6, it is very likely to meet offers priced below the hollowing middle, low confidence given no pricing on record.
